section.title: Narrative IDs
section.simpara: Each narrative (story, epic, tale, saga, or what-if) carries an id attribute that is a positive integer drawn from an internal sequential counter, independent of any external platform. The counter starts at 1 and increments with each new narrative, regardless of the identifier assigned on any hosting platform (e.g. GitHub, GitLab). The mapping between internal IDs and external platform issue references is recorded in documentation/06-change-control/trackers.xml.

section.title: Contributor IDs
section.simpara: Each contributor is assigned a platform-independent handle recorded as the xml:id attribute of their contributor.xml profile file and used as the contributor attribute value in release history files. The mapping between this handle and platform account URLs is maintained in documentation/07-contributions/trackers.xml.

section.title: Commit messages
section.simpara: The title line must not exceed 72 characters including the newline. All other lines must not exceed 80 characters including the newline. Every commit message has exactly one -- line describing the state before, one => line describing the state after, and at most one * line for optional additional information:
section.programlisting: Factorise reusable snippets from the vision document -- Other documents will have the same author, publisher, or introduction. => Extracted shareable fragments for reuse via XInclude. * Enhanced phrasing along the way. [Product Story 1]

section.title: Changelogs
section.simpara: Every file carries a changelog in a trailing XML comment. Each entry covers one story and follows this structure:
section.programlisting:
## <narrative-type> <narrative-id> — <date>
### Authors
- <full name>
### Agents
- Claude Code: Sonnet 4.6 - Codex: GPT-5.5
### Added
- <what was introduced>
section.simpara: ### Authors lists the people who worked on the entry. ### Agents immediately follows and lists any AI agents that contributed — name and version are sufficient. Authorship implies responsibility: an author can be contacted and held accountable for what they have written. AI agents cannot bear that responsibility, which is why they are recorded separately and omitted from commit messages. Omit ### Agents entirely when no agent contributed.

section.title: Time tracking
section.simpara: Every narrative level — tale, epic, story — and every activity iteration carries five time fields:

listitem.simpara: Expected effort, expressed as an ISO 8601 duration (e.g. PT8H, P3D).
Actual effort, expressed as an ISO 8601 duration.

section.simpara: These fields follow a V-model. Estimates are set top-down: a tale is estimated first, its epics next, then their stories, and finally each activity iteration. Actuals are recorded bottom-up: activity iterations are closed first, which informs the story's actuals, which in turn inform the epic's, and so on up to the tale. All five fields are optional and are filled in as work progresses.

Months and years are not used as duration units. When the estimated duration is under a year, record both time-estimate (weeks being the largest unit) and target-end. When the estimated duration is a year or more, record target-end only.
